title: Set guardrails, then choose the response
description: Adjust independent quality, cost, and latency limits, then change the evidence available to responders. The decision record shows when to continue, mitigate, roll back, or escalate evaluation.

evidenceLevels.label: Sparse production signal
evidenceLevels.detail: Few cases, delayed labels, and no controlled replay.

evidenceLevels.label: Slice-aware sample
evidenceLevels.detail: The affected slice is represented, but attribution is not yet reproduced.

evidenceLevels.label: Reproduced and attributed
evidenceLevels.detail: A paired replay identifies the candidate release as the changed boundary.

scenarios.label: Billing assistant release
scenarios.detail: A candidate prompt and retrieval route is serving 20% of billing traffic.
scenarios.isolatedCostMitigation: Route long contexts to the bounded summarization path.
scenarios.userImpact: Some users receive unsupported billing explanations and wait longer for them.

scenarios.label: Premium-model routing
scenarios.detail: A new router improves answer quality but sends too many low-risk tasks to the premium model.
scenarios.isolatedCostMitigation: Disable premium routing for low-risk intents and preserve it for evaluated hard cases.
scenarios.userImpact: Answers remain healthy, but budget burn shortens the service's operating runway.

scenarios.label: Order-tool timeouts
scenarios.detail: The model and prompt are stable, but a downstream order service is timing out.
scenarios.isolatedCostMitigation: Open the dependency circuit and return a truthful degraded response without retrying.
scenarios.userImpact: Order-status users wait through a timeout and retry before receiving a degraded answer.

scenarios.label: Healthy bounded canary
scenarios.detail: A new model route is serving 5% of low-risk support traffic.
scenarios.isolatedCostMitigation: Keep the existing exposure cap while evidence accumulates.
scenarios.userImpact: Measured outcomes remain inside every declared production boundary.
